In August 2021, Chao was elected to the board of directors of the [Kroger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kroger "Kroger") supermarket chain.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-IBTimes-ChaoKroger-100) In 2021, Chao also joined the Board of Trustees of the [John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_Center_for_the_Performing_Arts "John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts").[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-101) In 2024 she joined the board of directors of [Mobileye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobileye "Mobileye").[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-102)

In January 2023, Chao, in a statement provided to [Politico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politico "Politico") and [NBC News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC_News "NBC News"), rebuked Trump for a series of racist attacks on her during his [2024 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump_2024_presidential_campaign "Donald Trump 2024 presidential campaign").[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-103)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-McGraw_politico-104)[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-105)

## Second Trump administration

In January 2025, Trump appointed Chao to the [Kennedy Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Center "Kennedy Center") Board of Trustees.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-106)

## Controversies

In 2013, Super PAC [Progress Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progress_Kentucky "Progress Kentucky") stated in a tweet that Chao was Mitch McConnell's "Chinese wife" and that this "[m]ay explain why your job moved to China", linking to conspiracy theorist and radio host [Jeff Rense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Rense "Jeff Rense")'s website.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-107)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-108) After being criticized by Democrats and Republicans for racially insensitive tweets, Progress Kentucky apologized and deleted them.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-109) In 2014, the owner of a Democratic political consulting firm in Northern Kentucky responded to Mitch McConnell's remarks at a Republican breakfast by posting in her personal [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter") account that Chao "isn't from KY, she is Asian". The Kentucky Democratic Party denounced the tweet, and the owner deleted her Twitter account.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-110)

Critics have claimed that the Chao family's shipping company, [Foremost Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foremost_Group "Foremost Group"), has ties to China.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-bridge-92) From January 2018 to April 2019, 72% of the total tonnage of chartered cargo shipped by Foremost was shipped to and from China.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-bridge-92) During Mitch McConnell's reelection campaign in 2020, his Democratic opponent [Amy McGrath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amy_McGrath "Amy McGrath") accused McConnell of making "millions from China". *[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Washington_Post "The Washington Post")* called these claims "spurious" and rated them "three Pinocchios" out of a possible four, remarking that, although McConnell is one of the wealthiest senators in Congress, "The story of how McConnell got rich has nothing to do with Chinese trade deals, spycraft or the coronavirus. He simply married into a higher tax bracket."[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-111)

As Secretary of Transportation, Chao appeared in at least a dozen interviews with her 96-year-old father, [James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_S._C._Chao "James S. C. Chao"), the founder of her family's shipping company. Some media outlets said the appearances raised ethical concerns, as public officials are prohibited from using their office to profit others or themselves;[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-father-112) a report by the [Transportation Department's Inspector General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_Inspector_General_of_the_United_States_Department_of_Transportation "Office of Inspector General of the United States Department of Transportation"), released in March 2021, cited multiple instances where Chao's office had helped to promote her family's shipping business.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-misuse-113) The Inspector General had asked the Trump administration's Justice Department in December 2020 to consider a criminal investigation into Chao, but the DOJ denied the request.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-misuse-113) Federal disclosures cited by *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")* revealed a gift to Chao and her husband from Chao's father in 2017 valued between $5 million and $25 million.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-bridge-92)

Chao pledged in 2017 to divest into cash the "[deferred stock units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stock_based_compensation "Stock based compensation")" (non-transferrable stock equivalents) she had earned while she was on the board of directors of [Vulcan Materials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vulcan_Materials "Vulcan Materials")[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-divest-114) by April 2018.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-pledge-115)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-sell-116) After the *Wall Street Journal* and other major news outlets reported in late May 2019 that she was still holding the stock, worth $250,000 to $500,000, she sold it on June 3, 2019,[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-sell-116)[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-divest-114) for a gain of $50,000 since April 2018; a report by the Inspector General did "not identify any evidence of a financial conflict of interest".[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-sell-116)[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-117)

An October 2018 *[Politico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politico "Politico")* analysis found that Chao had more than 290 hours of appointments which were labelled as "private" during working hours on working days in the first 14 months of her tenure as Secretary of Transportation, which former Department of Transportation officials described as unusual. DoT officials stated that the "private" labeling existed to help ensure Chao's security.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-118)

In June 2019, *Politico* reported that in 2017 Chao had designated her aide Todd Inman as a special liaison "to help with grant applications and other priorities" for Transportation Department projects in the state of [Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky "Kentucky"), the only state to have such a liaison. Inman was to act as an intermediary between the department, local Kentucky officials, and Kentucky Senator Mitch McConnell, who is Chao's husband. This resulted in grants of at least $78 million for projects in Mitch McConnell strongholds [Boone County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boone_County,_Kentucky "Boone County, Kentucky") and [Owensboro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Owensboro "Owensboro"). Inman had worked on the 2008 and 2014 re-election campaigns of McConnell; McConnell and local officials brought up the grants when he announced in Owensboro in December 2018 that he was running for re-election in 2020. Inman later became Chao's chief of staff. However, the Inspector General "did not find any irregularities" with respect to grants benefitting Kentucky and saw awards to Kentucky that were "consistent with other States' results" and "did not find evidence of steering" and concluded that the investigation "did not uncover evidence that Mr. Inman influenced grant awards benefiting Kentucky or gave Kentucky applicants an improper advantage".[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-119)

In May 2020, the Trump administration removed the acting Inspector General of the Transportation Department, [Mitch Behm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitch_Behm "Mitch Behm"). Behm, who was not a political appointee, was conducting an investigation into whether Secretary Elaine Chao was giving preferential treatment to projects in Kentucky. Her husband, Mitch McConnell, is the Senator of Kentucky and faced a re-election bid at the time.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-120)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-121) Trump appointed Howard "Skip" Elliott as interim Inspector General of the Transportation Department to replace Behm. However, at the same time, Elliott served as the head of one of the DoT's agencies, a role where Chao was his boss. Thus, Elliott had been put in charge of an office that was investigating his own actions and those of Chao.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-122)

In September 2019, the Democratic-controlled House of Representatives [Committee on Oversight and Reform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Committee_on_Oversight_and_Reform "Committee on Oversight and Reform") began an investigation into whether she used political office to benefit her family's business interests.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-123)[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-124) A September 16 letter from the Oversight committee to Chao documented allegations that the Department of Transportation was forced to cancel a trip to China in 2017 that Chao had planned to take because State Department ethics officials challenged her attempts to include her family members in official meetings with the Chinese government. The trip was canceled due to scheduling issues and no ethics charges were sustained.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-125)

On March 4, 2021, the Inspector General released their report regarding numerous ethics violations,[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-127)[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-128) including using department resources for personal errands and for promoting her father's biography.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-chao_npr-129) It also stated that it had referred its investigation to the Justice Department and the [U.S. Attorney's Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Attorney's_Office "U.S. Attorney's Office") in Washington D.C. for criminal prosecution in December 2020. Both declined to open criminal investigations into Chao.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-130)[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-131)

## Awards and honorary degrees

Chao holds 38 [honorary doctorates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honorary_doctorates "Honorary doctorates"),[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-132) including an honorary [Doctor of Humane Letters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_of_Humane_Letters "Doctor of Humane Letters") from Georgetown [McDonough School of Business](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McDonough_School_of_Business "McDonough School of Business") in 2015.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-133) She was initiated into [Omicron Delta Kappa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omicron_Delta_Kappa "Omicron Delta Kappa") at [SUNY Plattsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SUNY_Plattsburgh "SUNY Plattsburgh") as an *honoris causa* initiate in 1996.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-134) In 2006, inaugural class of winner of the [Great Immigrants Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Immigrants_Award "Great Immigrants Award") named by [Carnegie Corporation of New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnegie_Corporation_of_New_York "Carnegie Corporation of New York").[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-135) In 2024 she received the [Herman Kahn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herman_Kahn "Herman Kahn") Award for her lifetime contributions to society.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-136)

In 2026, Chao was recognized as the sponsor and "Godmother" of the U.S. maritime training ship *[State of Maine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_Maine_(ship) "State of Maine (ship)")*, which will be used at the [Maine Maritime Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine_Maritime_Academy "Maine Maritime Academy").[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-137)

## Personal life

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/Mitch_McConnell_and_Elaine_Chao_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Mitch_McConnell_and_Elaine_Chao_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mitch_McConnell_and_Elaine_Chao_(cropped).jpg)Chao and her husband, [Mitch McConnell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitch_McConnell "Mitch McConnell")

In 1993, Chao married [Mitch McConnell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitch_McConnell "Mitch McConnell"), [U.S. Senator from Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_senators_from_Kentucky "List of United States senators from Kentucky").[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-girding-138)

The [University of Louisville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Louisville "University of Louisville")'s Ekstrom Library opened the "McConnell-Chao Archives" in November 2009. It is a major component of the university's [McConnell Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McConnell_Center "McConnell Center").[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-139)[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-140)

From July 2022 onward, Trump had criticized McConnell's leadership on social media and directed attacks at Chao, including calling her "Coco Chow," which was widely condemned as racist. In a statement to [Politico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politico "Politico") in January 2023, Chao said that people had "deliberately misspelled or mispronounced my name. Asian Americans have worked hard to change that experience for the next generation. He doesn't seem to understand that, which says a whole lot more about him than it will ever say about Asian Americans."[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-McGraw_politico-104)[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-141)

Chao was traveling in China for a long-planned philanthropic visit when her husband [experienced cardiac arrest and was hospitalized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitch_McConnell#hospitalization2026 "Mitch McConnell") on June 14, 2026. She returned to the US on July 7. Her spokesperson said, "The Senator's health did not warrant an immediate return to the US."[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-142)

### Campaigning

In the two years leading up to the [2014 U.S. Senate elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_U.S._Senate_elections "2014 U.S. Senate elections"), during which time Chao was not in public office, Chao "headlined fifty of her own events and attended hundreds more with and on behalf of" her husband and was seen as "a driving force of his reelection campaign" and eventual victory over [Democratic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)") candidate [Alison Lundergan Grimes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alison_Lundergan_Grimes "Alison Lundergan Grimes"), who had portrayed McConnell as "anti-woman".[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-secret-143) After winning the election, McConnell said, "The biggest asset I have by far is the only Kentucky woman who served in a [president's cabinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_the_United_States "Cabinet of the United States"), my wife, Elaine Chao."[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-144)

She has been described by Jan Karzen, a longtime friend of McConnell's, as adding "a softer touch" to McConnell's style by speaking of him "in a feminine, wifely way".[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-girding-138) Chao has also been described as "the campaign hugger".[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-secret-143) *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")* described her as "unapologetically ambitious".[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-girding-138)

Chao's father has donated "millions of dollars" to the Chao-McConnell family.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-bridge-92) Chao's extended family has given more than a million dollars to McConnell's campaigns.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-bridge-92) The extended family is also a top contributor to the [Republican Party of Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_of_Kentucky "Republican Party of Kentucky"), giving it approximately $525,000 over two decades.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-bridge-92)

Chao") met [Taiwanese President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiwanese_President "Taiwanese President") [Tsai Ing-wen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsai_Ing-wen "Tsai Ing-wen") at the [Presidential Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_Office_Building,_Taiwan "Presidential Office Building, Taiwan") in Taipei, [Taiwan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiwan "Taiwan"), in 2016.

Chao has five younger sisters, including [Angela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Chao "Angela Chao"), former CEO of the Foremost Group.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-ruth-145)[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-voyage-146) Angela died in February 2024.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-147)

Chao's sister Grace is married to [Gordon Hartogensis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gordon_Hartogensis "Gordon Hartogensis") who served as director of the [Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pension_Benefit_Guaranty_Corporation "Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation") (PBGC), a part of the Labor Department, in May 2019.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-148)[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-in-laws-149)[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-150)[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-confirmed-151) Hartogensis co-founded forecasting-software company Petrolsoft in 1989, which was purchased for $60 million by Aspen Technology in 2000.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-in-laws-149) He founded and led application software company Auric Technology LLC until it was sold to a company based in Mexico in 2011 and then helped govern the Hartogensis Family Trust.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-confirmed-151)[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-in-laws-149)

In April 2008, Chao's father gave Chao and McConnell between $5 million and $25 million.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-152)[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-153)[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-fang-154)

In 2012, the Chao family donated $40 million to [Harvard Business School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_Business_School "Harvard Business School") for scholarships to students of Chinese heritage and for the Ruth Mulan Chu Chao Center, an [executive education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_education "Executive education") building named for Chao's late mother.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-155)[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-156) It is the first Harvard Business School building named after a woman[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-157) and the first building named after an American of Asian ancestry.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-158) [Ruth Mulan Chu Chao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruth_Mulan_Chu_Chao "Ruth Mulan Chu Chao") returned to school at age 51 to earn a master's degree in [Asian literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_literature "Asian literature") and [history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Asia "History of Asia") from [St. John's University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._John's_University_(New_York_City) "St. John's University (New York City)") in the [Queens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens "Queens") [borough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borough_(New_York_City) "Borough (New York City)") of New York City.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-ruth-145)

Elaine Chao, along with the Chao family, is Christian.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao#cite_note-159)
